self_assessment: Replaced lib/srv/db/aws.go with lib/srv/db/ca.go. initCACert still returns early when the CA is already configured, now bails out for anything that is not RDS/Redshift/CloudSQL so self-hosted databases never trigger a download, then gets the cert via getCACert and only assigns it after tlsca.ParseCertificatePEM confirms it is valid x509. getCACert caches per instance: it stats <dataDir>/<server name>.ca, reads and returns it when present, otherwise calls cfg.CADownloader.Download and writes the result with teleport.FileMaskOwnerOnly. Added the CADownloader interface (Download(ctx, types.DatabaseServer) ([]byte, error)), NewRealDownloader(dataDir) and the realDownloader struct holding dataDir plus an http.Client; its Download switches on server.GetType() to downloadForRDS (region-aware URL table), downloadForRedshift and the new downloadForCloudSQL, and returns a BadParameter error for anything else. downloadForCloudSQL calls the GCP SQL Admin API Instances.Get for the configured project/instance, wraps failures with guidance about needing the Cloud SQL Admin role or cloudsql.instances.get permission (or setting ca_cert_file), and returns NotFound when the instance carries no ServerCaCert. Config gained a CADownloader field defaulting to NewRealDownloader(DataDir) in CheckAndSetDefaults. Verified: go build ./... and go vet ./lib/srv/db/... clean, plus a scratch test with a counting fake downloader confirming the self-hosted server gets no cert and no download, RDS/Redshift/CloudSQL each get the cert with exactly three downloads, a second init pass downloads nothing, and a fresh server object with the same name reads the cached file instead of re-downloading. The package's existing tests panic identically before and after my change (json-iterator/reflect2 against Go 1.24), so they could not be exercised.
